vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: ai-persona-os
Version: 1.3.3

The OpenClaw AgentSkills bundle is designed to provide a robust 'operating system' for AI agents, focusing on reliability, context management, and security. The included shell scripts (`scripts/*.sh`) perform local file system operations for setup, validation, daily operations, and security audits, without evidence of malicious execution or data exfiltration. The cron job payloads (`assets/cron-payloads/*.sh`) utilize `openclaw cron add` for persistence, but the instructions provided to the AI agent are for legitimate maintenance and reporting tasks. Crucially, the documentation, particularly `SKILL.md`, `assets/SECURITY-template.md`, and `references/security-patterns.md`, explicitly addresses prompt injection, credential handling, and secure communication, instructing the AI agent on how to defend against these attacks, rather than facilitating them. There is no clear evidence of intentional harmful behavior.

llm.summary: The skill's files and runtime instructions broadly match an 'agent OS' purpose, but there are important inconsistencies and execution risks (shell scripts/cron templates that expect an OpenClaw CLI and will modify workspace state) that you should review before running.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (an 'OS' for agents) aligns with the delivered templates, templates for HEARTBEAT/ESCALATION/SECURITY, and multiple helper scripts; those artifacts are appropriate for the stated purpose. However, the SKILL metadata declares no required binaries while many assets and cron templates invoke an 'openclaw' CLI and reference a model name (e.g., --model opus). The omission of that dependency in the metadata is an inconsistency.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs the agent to inspect the user's workspace and, if files are missing, to run ./scripts/setup-wizard.sh. The repository includes multiple shell scripts and cron-add templates that will modify workspace files, schedule jobs (openclaw cron add), read/write archive and memory files, and can be executed by the user/agent. This is coherent with the stated purpose but grants the skill the ability to run arbitrary shell code when the scripts are executed — the docs do not warn users to inspect the scripts first nor declare the external CLI dependency required to safely run them.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only), which is low risk by itself. But the package includes many shell scripts (setup-wizard.sh, security-audit.sh, cron payloads) that will be written to disk as part of the skill payload. There is no download-from-URL behavior, but included scripts may be executed locally — review them before running.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill doesn't request environment variables or credentials in metadata, and most templates explicitly advise safe credential handling. That said, templates reference external services (Discord, Slack) and the openclaw CLI; if you wire those up you will need credentials — the skill does not declare or request them up front, which is appropriate but means you must supply/confirm any credentials before enabling external features.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (normal). The skill includes cron job templates that instruct adding scheduled tasks via the openclaw CLI; if executed, those commands create persistent scheduled behavior. Autonomous model invocation is allowed by default (disable-model-invocation:false) — that's platform normal but increases the blast radius if the cron jobs or scripts are misused. The skill does not request to modify other skills or global agent settings in its metadata.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to be a coherent 'agent OS' with many helpful templates and scripts, but treat the included shell scripts and cron templates as code you must inspect before running. Specific actions to take before installing/using: 1) Verify you have the required CLI/tools (the scripts and cron templates call an 'openclaw' CLI and reference models) or adjust scripts accordingly. 2) Open and review scripts/setup-wizard.sh and scripts/security-audit.sh for any commands you don't expect (network calls, remote downloads, or destructive file operations) before executing them. 3) If you plan to wire external channels (Discord/Slack/email), only provide credentials you trust and follow the SECURITY.md confirmation flows. 4) Prefer running the setup and audit scripts in an isolated workspace or sandbox first. 5) Verify the author/homepage and consider pulling this into source control so you can review and revert changes. These inconsistencies (undeclared CLI dependency + executable scripts that modify state) are why I mark it 'suspicious' rather than 'benign'. If you want, I can summarize the top sections of scripts/setup-wizard.sh and security-audit.sh so you can assess them quickly.
